perField.evidenceAnswer: Evidence = how the sample result (p̂) compares to the expected value. Is p̂ above or below what we'd expect if the claim were false?
perField.explanationAnswer: There are always exactly two explanations: (1) the result happened by CHANCE alone, or (2) there is a REAL effect.
perField.convincingAnswer: If the probability of getting the result by chance alone is small (roughly less than 5%), the evidence IS convincing.
perField.convincingExplain: Reference the simulation: 'Because ___ out of ___ simulations produced results this extreme, it is [likely/unlikely] to happen by chance alone.'
perField.procedureAnswer: Ask: How many samples? (one) What data type? (proportion) What's the goal? (estimate with CI) → One-sample z-interval for p.
perField.conditionsMet: Three conditions: (1) Random sample, (2) n ≤ 10% of N, (3) np̂ ≥ 10 AND n(1−p̂) ≥ 10. ALL must be met.
perField.conditionsExplain: Show the numbers for each: Random? ✓/✗. 10%: n = ___ ≤ 10% of N = ___? Large counts: np̂ = ___ ≥ 10? n(1−p̂) = ___ ≥ 10?
perField.seAnswer: SE(p̂) = √(p̂(1−p̂)/n). Plug in the sample proportion and sample size.
perField.meAnswer: Margin of error = z* × SE(p̂). Multiply the critical value by the standard error.
perField.ciLower: Lower bound = p̂ − (margin of error) = p̂ − z* × √(p̂(1−p̂)/n)
perField.ciUpper: Upper bound = p̂ + (margin of error) = p̂ + z* × √(p̂(1−p̂)/n)
perField.sampleSizeAnswer: Solve: n ≥ p̂(1−p̂) × (z*/ME)². Use p̂ = 0.5 if no prior estimate. Always round UP!
perField.capstoneConditions: Check: (1) Random? (2) n ≤ 10% of N? (3) Both np̂ ≥ 10 and n(1−p̂) ≥ 10?
perField.capstoneExplain: Template: 'We are __% confident that the interval from ___ to ___ captures the true proportion of [context].'
perField.ciInterpretation: Template: 'We are __% confident that the interval from ___ to ___ captures the true proportion of [context].' Include all three elements!
perField.claimAnswer: If ALL values in the CI are consistent with the claim → convincing evidence. If ANY value is inconsistent → not convincing evidence.
perField.claimExplain: Reference whether the claim value falls inside or outside the interval. If the entire CI is above/below the threshold, that's convincing evidence.
perField.confLevelAnswer: The confidence level describes the long-run success rate of the METHOD, not the probability for a single interval. Think: repeated sampling.
perField.factorAnswer: ME = z* × √(p̂(1−p̂)/n). Larger n → smaller ME. Higher confidence → larger z* → larger ME. Width = 2 × ME.
perField.cap63Interpret: Template: 'We are __% confident that the interval from ___ to ___ captures the true proportion of [context].'
perField.cap63Justify: Check if the claim value falls entirely inside or outside the CI range.
perField.cap63JustifyExplain: State whether ALL values in the interval are consistent or inconsistent with the claim, and why.
perField.nullAnswer: The null hypothesis is always H₀: p = [claimed value]. It uses '=' and the parameter p (not p̂).
perField.altAnswer: Look for keywords: 'greater/more/higher' → p > p₀, 'less/fewer/lower' → p < p₀, 'different/differs/changed' → p ≠ p₀.
perField.nullHypothesis: Format: H₀: p = [value]. The null always contains '=' and uses p (the population proportion), never p̂.
perField.altHypothesis: Format: Hₐ: p [< or > or ≠] [value]. The direction comes from the research question. Use p, not p̂.
perField.paramDef: Define p as 'the proportion of ALL [population] who [would do something].' Use 'all' and 'would' to indicate population, not sample.
perField.errorAnswer: Common errors: using p̂ instead of p, putting inequality in H₀, wrong direction for Hₐ, defining parameter with sample language.
perField.testAnswer: Testing a claim about ONE proportion? → One-sample z-test. Estimating? → z-interval. Two groups? → Two-sample.
perField.testConditionsMet: Three conditions: (1) Random sample, (2) n ≤ 10% of N, (3) np₀ ≥ 10 AND n(1−p₀) ≥ 10. Use p₀, NOT p̂!
perField.testConditionsExplain: Show: Random? 10%: n = ___ ≤ 10% of N? Large counts: np₀ = n×p₀ = ___ ≥ 10? n(1−p₀) = ___ ≥ 10? Use the NULL value p₀!
perField.cap64Null: H₀: p = [claimed value]. Always uses '=' sign.
perField.cap64Alt: Hₐ: p [direction] [value]. Direction from the research question.
perField.cap64ParamDef: p = the proportion of ALL [population] who [would do something].
perField.cap64Procedure: One categorical variable, one sample, testing a claim → One-sample z-test for a population proportion.
perField.cap64ConditionsMet: Check all three: Random, 10%, Large counts (using p₀).
perField.cap64ConditionsWork: Show calculations: np₀ = ___ and n(1−p₀) = ___. Remember to use p₀ from the null hypothesis, not the sample proportion!
perField.zStatAnswer: z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1−p₀)/n). Use p₀ in the denominator because we assume H₀ is true.
perField.pvalueAnswer: For Ha: p > p₀, find P(Z ≥ z). For Ha: p < p₀, find P(Z ≤ z). For Ha: p ≠ p₀, find 2 × P(Z ≥ |z|).
perField.pvalueInterpretation: Template: 'Assuming [null is true], there is a [p-value] probability of getting a sample proportion of [p̂] or [more extreme] by chance alone in a random sample of [n] from [population].'
perField.directionAnswer: Ha: p > p₀ → right tail. Ha: p < p₀ → left tail. Ha: p ≠ p₀ → both tails (double the one-tail area).
perField.cap65Null: H₀: p = [claimed value]. Always uses '=' sign.
perField.cap65Alt: Hₐ: p [direction] [value]. Direction from the research question.
perField.cap65ZStat: z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1−p₀)/n). Use p₀ in the standard deviation.
perField.cap65PValue: Match the tail direction to Ha. One-sided: single tail. Two-sided: double the one-tail area.
perField.cap65Interpret: Include: (1) assume H₀ true, (2) the p-value probability, (3) sample proportion 'or more extreme', (4) 'by chance alone', (5) context.
perField.compareAnswer: Compare the p-value to α. If p-value ≤ α, reject H₀. If p-value > α, fail to reject H₀.
perField.decisionAnswer: If p-value ≤ α → reject H₀ (convincing evidence for Ha). If p-value > α → fail to reject H₀ (not convincing evidence for Ha). Never 'accept H₀' or 'prove Ha'.
perField.conclusionText: Template: 'Because the p-value of ___ is [less than / greater than] α = ___, we [reject / fail to reject] H₀. There [is / is not] convincing statistical evidence that [Ha in context].' Must explicitly compare p-value to α, state the decision, and state the conclusion about Ha in context.
perField.conclusionErrorAnswer: Common errors: (1) accepting H₀ instead of failing to reject, (2) saying 'proves' Ha is true, (3) not comparing p-value to α explicitly, (4) concluding about H₀ instead of Ha, (5) no context.
perField.fullTestNull: H₀: p = [claimed value]. Always uses '=' sign.
perField.fullTestAlt: Hₐ: p [direction] [value]. Direction from the research question.
perField.fullTestZStat: z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1−p₀)/n). Use p₀ in the denominator.
perField.fullTestPValue: Match the tail direction to Ha. One-sided: single tail. Two-sided: double the one-tail area.
perField.fullTestConclusion: Because the p-value of ___ is [comparison] α = ___, we [decision]. There [is/is not] convincing statistical evidence that [Ha in context].
perField.cap66Null: H₀: p = [claimed value]. Always uses '=' sign.
perField.cap66Alt: Hₐ: p [direction] [value]. Direction from the research question.
perField.cap66ParamDef: p = the proportion of ALL [population] who [would do something].
perField.cap66ZStat: z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1−p₀)/n). Use p₀ in the standard deviation.
perField.cap66PValue: Match the tail direction to Ha. One-sided: single tail. Two-sided: double the one-tail area.
perField.cap66Conclusion: Include all four elements: (1) explicit p-value to α comparison, (2) reject/fail to reject decision, (3) conclusion about Ha, (4) context.
perField.errorTypeAnswer: Type I = reject a true H₀ (false positive). Type II = fail to reject a false H₀ (false negative).
perField.type1Interpretation: Type I means finding convincing evidence for Ha when H₀ is actually true. Rewrite Ha in context, then say the true proportion is still the null value.
perField.type2Interpretation: Type II means not finding convincing evidence for Ha when Ha is actually true. Say the study misses a real effect.
perField.powerInterpretation: Power = probability of correctly rejecting a false H₀. Template: 'If the true proportion is ___, there is a ___ probability that we find convincing evidence that...'
perField.powerFactorAnswer: Power increases when n increases, α increases, standard error decreases, or the true parameter is farther from the null value.
perField.cap67Type1: State the alternative in context, then say reality was actually the null value. This is a false positive.
perField.cap67Type2: State that the study did not find convincing evidence, then say the alternative was actually true. This is a false negative.
perField.cap67Consequential: Think about the consequence of each mistake. Which error would cause the bigger real-world loss or harm?
perField.cap67Justify: Describe what happens after each error, then explain why one leads to the more serious consequence.
perField.alphaType1Prob: The significance level is the probability of a Type I error, so P(Type I error) = α exactly.
perField.powerDefinitionAnswer: Power is the probability that a test correctly rejects a false H₀. It is also 1 - P(Type II error).
perField.alphaTradeoffAnswer: Smaller α lowers the chance of a Type I error, but it raises the chance of a Type II error and lowers power. Larger α does the opposite.
perField.alphaChoiceAnswer: If a Type I error would be especially serious, use a smaller α. If missing a real effect is the bigger concern, a larger α may be more reasonable.
perField.twoPropProcedureAnswer: Two groups + categorical data + confidence interval = two-sample z-interval for a difference in proportions.
perField.twoPropConditionsMet: Check: two independent random samples or random assignment, the 10% condition for each sample when sampling without replacement, and four counts (x1, n1-x1, x2, n2-x2) all at least 10.
perField.twoPropConditionsExplain: State whether the data came from two random samples or a randomized experiment. If sampling, check n1 ≤ 10%N1 and n2 ≤ 10%N2. Then check successes and failures in both groups are each at least 10.
perField.twoPropMEAnswer: ME = z* × √[(p̂₁(1-p̂₁)/n₁) + (p̂₂(1-p̂₂)/n₂)]. Use the sample proportions from each group.
perField.twoPropCIInterpretation: Template: 'We are __% confident that the true difference (group 1 minus group 2) in proportions is between ___ and ___.' Translate the interval into percentage points and include the context.
